title: How Languages Work: An Introduction to Language Study

questions.question: Which level of language deals with how words are built from meaningful parts?
questions.rationale: Morphology handles word-building: 'un-break-able' contains three meaningful units (morphemes).

questions.question: Saying 'Can you pass the salt?' to make a request belongs to which level?
questions.rationale: Pragmatics is meaning in context — the sentence is grammatically a question but functionally a request.

questions.question: English 'father', Latin 'pater', and Sanskrit 'pitṛ' are examples of:
questions.rationale: Cognates are words descended from a common ancestor — evidence that these languages belong to one family (Indo-European).

questions.question: Devanagari, where consonant letters carry a default vowel that can be overridden, is classified as:
questions.rationale: Abugidas (like Devanagari) write consonants with an inherent vowel, marking other vowels with diacritics.

questions.question: Which study strategy does research on memory most strongly support?
options: Four hours of study once a week
questions.rationale: Consistency beats intensity: reviewing at spaced intervals just before you would forget strengthens memory through repeated retrieval.

questions.question: The fact that 'The dog bit the man' means something different from 'The man bit the dog' illustrates which level of language?
questions.rationale: Syntax handles sentence structure — reordering the same words changes who bites whom.

questions.question: 'Bank' meaning a riverside versus 'bank' meaning a financial institution falls under which level?
questions.rationale: Semantics deals with meaning — these two senses of 'bank' show how one word can carry multiple meanings.

questions.question: Tamil and Telugu belong to which language family?
questions.rationale: Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam are listed as members of the Dravidian family.

questions.question: Arabic script, where letters mainly represent consonants, is classified as:
questions.rationale: Abjads write letters mainly for consonants — like Arabic and Hebrew; logographies like Chinese write whole words/morphemes.

questions.question: What does the strategy 'comprehensible input' mean?
options: Reading and listening slightly above your current level
Avoiding listening until speaking is mastered
questions.rationale: Comprehensible input means consuming language material just above your level — hard enough to stretch you but still understandable.
